chapter: Don Redman's band at Connie's Inn
title: The Woodside Hotel and the arrival of Basie's and Hawkins's bands
summary: Living at the Woodside Hotel, the Black musicians' hotel, he saw Basie's band check in from Kansas City around 1936 and Erskine Hawkins's soon after.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So when I came back I was living in the Woodside Hotel in New York. A lot of musicians lived there, you know, in those days.
Yeah, that was the black musicians' hotel.
Like the President was for the white musicians in New York.
That's right, that's right. And, gee whiz, Count Basie's band stayed in there. Erskine Hawkin(s) band. I was standing out in front of the hotel when Erskine's band drove up from Alabama /state.
And I was there when Basie's band
checked in from Kansas City, too.
And that was about 1937, I guess
